DEIRDRE LARKIN Life Begins at 90

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
World record holder Deirdre Larkin is running into her 90's with a brand new role.

Unique Selling Point:
What would you like to do on your 90th birthday? How about a brisk 10km run?
In 2017 Carte Blanche took Deirdre to Switzerland to compete in the Geneva half marathon. She ran a magnificent race and broke her own world record by 5 minutes! But our galloping granny still had a dream: to complete 10 Two Oceans Marathons and be awarded her “blue number”. This would have happened in April 2021. Unfortunately the Covid-19 pandemic put an end to that dream - not because Deirdre isn’t raring to go - but because the race was last held in 2019. Deirdre completed her 8th Two Oceans marathon that year (in a time of 02:47) and has since been stalled by lockdown.

But, she is still running!

I think it would be good to do a short update about her and share the news with people that life can even start at 90!

Summary:
With a strict regime of teaching piano at St Peter’s during the week, and running races on the weekends, Deirdre made old age about fun, learning and achievement. But she finally retired from teaching in 2019, and the pandemic robbed her of the thrill of competition. Without a sense of purpose any octogenarian finds life a struggle, and like every runner, she has struggled in lockdown with no races to run. But she never gave up.

This extraordinary woman turns 90 on Heritage Day and has just been appointed a brand ambassador for running club RunZone. This has changed her life completely! Her new role has given her purpose and now she always has something to look forward to. They hold time trials, club races, training events and online training 6 days a week. RunZone is really about living a healthy lifestyle and they are including Deirdre in a lot of programmes. They have even created the Larkin Healthy Living programme which has just been rolled outt. This is a Legacy programme so that she will always be remembered.


Further information:
Time spent in the company of this remarkable woman is both inspirational and entertaining. With her no-nonsense approach and sharp insights she gives fresh perspective on the daily challenges that we all have to face - not only runners. Irrepressibly positive about enjoying life, Deirdre is itching to hear the sound of the Two Oceans starting gun in 2022!

Extra Budget Items:
Sonja's interview is in Somerset West, but would prefer to send Tim Wege to do the interview rather than a Zoom interview. Perhaps no extra budget required.

Script:


DEIRDRE TURNS 90

V/O: Heritage Day marked a very special occasion in Johannesburg.

Graham: This is Deirdre, she turns 90 years young today!

Crowd: Cheers

Graham: She is still the current word champion for 85 plus for 10 km, and it was a sub-60. She did 54 minutes at the age of 85.

Sfx: Happy birthday dear Deirdre, happy birthday to you. Hip, hip hooray! Yay!
(Starts race)

V/O: In 2017 Carte Blanche met 85-year-old Deirdre Larkin - a piano teacher who only started running at the age of 78 and discovered a natural talent for the sport. She quickly started breaking records for the 10k distance. But when we first filmed her at a half marathon in Pretoria, she smashed the world record for her age group by a staggering 20 minutes. Inspired by this remarkable athlete, Supersport and M-Net sponsored Deirdre’s trip to Switzerland to compete in the Geneva Half Marathon.

Derek: Beautiful city, isn’t it?

Deirdre: Yes, it is! But it’s all so different I don’t know what’s happening next. I’m just in one state of excitement all the time.

V/O: When race day dawned Deirdre got down to business. Not only did she run a personal best and do South Africa proud, she astonished everyone by taking another 7 minutes off her world record.

Link: In Geneva I was really bowled over by Deirdre’s energy and love for life, and of course her incredible performance. And now four years later we’re going to catch up with her for her 90th birthday.

Derek: Hallo! Happy birthday – am I allowed to give you a hug?

Deirdre: Ninety sounds a terrible age!

V/O: She still lives in her own home and runs every day: 5k’s during the week, and 10 or 15 on weekends.

Derek: But Deirdre how do you feel after a 15k run?

Deirdre: Well, I feel that I’ve had enough running, but I feel exhilarated.

Derek: But after 15k’s how are those muscles and joints?

Deirdre: Well, they’re fine. They don’t notice it because I run regularly. If I stopped for a couple of months then of course they would complain.

V/O Deirdre trained as a concert pianist and taught music for over 60 years. She finally retired at the tender age of 88.

Derek: Would you ever consider moving into a retirement home?

Deirdre: No, no. No I would hate to live in a retirement home. No thank you very much. And I’ve seen enough of them. Yes, because when I had a musical group we often played at retirement homes, and there’s an air about them. I am sure it increases your age by at least 20 years.

V/O: Another big change in Deirdre’s life is that her daughter Catherine has moved back home with her mother.

Catherine: With lockdown, isolation was a real issue, particularly in the early days. She didn’t see anyone for literally weeks on end. She would, when she could run, she would run by herself, and she just said she was a bit lonely, a bit isolated.

Derek: What have you learned?

Catherine: What my weak points are! She doesn’t tolerate self-pity or that kind of thing, so being with her can be good because she’s always focused on something good happening, or some event, some purpose.

Derek: Deirdre there were those tough weeks of hard lockdown. How did it affect you?

Deirdre: Well fortunately I’ve got a large garden so I could go running round the garden, which I did. But the only trouble is we’ve got about 4 plovers who live down at the bottom of the garden, and every time I passed them: grrrrrr! It was their territory. What was I doing there?

Derek: So even lockdown didn’t get you down?

Deirdre: No, no, no not at all

Derek: The big question Have you been vaccinated?

Deirdre: Yes, I've been vaccinated twice. No side effects, and no Covid!

Derek: Deirdre seriously, what is more difficult, what is tough about getting older?

Deirdre: Well, people treat you more and more as though you’re senile. Just kind of – not a lack of respect – but people think you can’t do things.

Derek: And you like proving them wrong?

Deirdre: I try to. Yes, yes, I’m just waiting for the day when you say oh, not allowed to drive a car. But I believe there’s no age restriction is there yet?

Derek: So you’re still driving?

Deidre: I’m still driving, yes.

V/O: What’s more, she has a new career as a brand ambassador for Run Zone Athletics Club.

Derek: And now she’s the poster girl for Run Zone?

Graham: Yes she is – and not centrefold though, but yes!.

V/O: Chairman Graham Block explains.

Graham: She’s amazingly popular on our runs. And it’s not only just her as a person, it’s the consistency, the consistency of her running; her pace of running is what gets people also going. We have younger people trying to keep up with her and they can’t. And those are the sort of things that motivate them, and she becomes their goal in the sense of – we want to try and keep up with her and catch up with her.

Deidre: Run Zone has encouraged me so much, and they’ve given, they gave me my clothes. They look after me, so I’m running as long as I can with Run Zone.

Sonja: I think it’s fantastic at this age to actually be sponsored: you know, new shoes and kit and everything. I mean my sponsor dropped me long time ago!

V/O: One of Deirdre’s biggest fans is running legend Sonja Laxton. The first woman to be awarded triple Springbok colours in track, road and cross country, she’s now 73 and still running.

Derek: Is this just genetics, and just having the right body shape?

Sonja: I think you must be born to be a top runner. Perhaps the right muscle fibres and the right genes, and I think the mental attitude helps as well. But she’s been given this wonderful talent, which unfortunately she only discovered at 78. And I shudder to think what she would have done if she’d started earlier – say at the age of 20, 25. I think she would have gone to the Olympics over and over again.

V/O: Deidre’s ambition was to run 10 Two Oceans half marathons to get her blue number. She managed to do 8 before the pandemic intervened and all races were cancelled.

Deidre: I hope one day I can do another one, another half marathon.

Graham: She’s on eight at the moment, and we’re going to do everything in our best that we can and will do to get her there to complete it.

Derek: And take a little bit of sparkling wine with you to celebrate.

Derek: I remember every night in Geneva you’d insist on a little glass of wine?

Deidre: Oh yes, I must have my glass of wine, white wine. Yes. Preferably sparkling.

Derek: You think that’s part of the formula?

Deidre: Maybe yes. There is Graham Block who runs Run Zone, and then there’s Graham Beck. Two of my favourite men.

V/O: And now that she’s in the 90 plus category, a new world record is almost a certainty.
